sample_unit: synthetic ICU records across three non-IID hospital clients plus PhysioNet-based external dataset
models_evaluated: Federated decision-tree ensemble with Performance-Based Filtering (PBF)

links.outcome: Critical-class recall under label-flipping poisoning attack, PBF versus FedAvg, Krum, Trimmed Mean, Coordinate Median
links.effect: Under a targeted label-flipping attack, PBF achieved 86.79% accuracy and 0.904 critical-class recall; PBF gave stronger protection of critical-class recall than the comparison aggregation methods.
links.quote: Comparative evaluation against FedAvg, Krum, Trimmed Mean, and Coordinate Median shows that PBF provides stronger protection of critical-class recall under adversarial conditions, although full prospective clinical validation remains outside the scope of this study.

unlisted_practices: Performance-based filtering of poisoned client updates in federated learning
Post-quantum key encapsulation (ML-KEM-512) with AES-256-GCM for model update exchange
Edge-hosted lightweight patient-state digital twin for ICU monitoring

screen.reason: Empirical study testing performance-based filtering (PBF) against adversarial label-poisoning attacks in a federated learning architecture for ICU patient risk monitoring.
